text:
ops-bot: INCIDENT: surge of CUDA errors + OOM kills observed in inference-pool-3 (hostgroup: ap-east-1-gpu-*.svc). alert_id=INC-2024-1719994321 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: summary: ~20% of active nodes reporting repeated 'NVRM: GPU X: GPU has fallen off the bus' + dmesg Xid 31/15/13 patterns; container restarts and model-serving OOMs. Preliminary customer impact: elevated latency for hosted endpoints, some 503s.

raj_oncall: Ack. I'm booting into triage. First pass: isolate noisy hosts and start evacuation.

emma_ops: Thanks Raj. Can you paste the top dmesg snippet and nvidia-smi from an affected host?

raj_oncall: Pasting from host ap-east-1-gpu-07 (trimmed):
```
[ 10234.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=4210, GPU=0
[ 10235.234567] kernel: oom-kill: Kill process 5421 (runtimesrv) score 142 or sacrifice child
[ 10235.234680] containerd: container runtime exited with status 137
```
```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR
GPU 0
  Product Name                    : A100-SXM4-40GB
  ECC Errors
    Volatile Uncorr. ECC         : 24
    Volatile Corr. ECC           : 180
```

leo_sre: That's a classic thermal/driver noise -> soft-reset loop. Could be KV cache pressure causing mem fragmentation then OOM on the runtime process.

sara_infra: On the infra side I'm watching k8s node conditions. Several nodes hit MemoryPressure and kubelet evicted pods. Node autoproc shows repeated kubelet restart on ap-east-1-gpu-07/09/11.

marta_eng: Product support reports about 12 customer requests spiking with slow tokens. Putting a customer bridge on hold until we stabilize. product-support: please gather customer IDs.

product-support: Putting impacted customers into internal bridge: cust-324, cust-847, cust-209. We'll open a postmortem channel if this is sustained.

raj_oncall: Mitigation plan (quick):
1) cordon ap-east-1-gpu-07,09,11
2) drain with --delete-local-data and pod disruption budget bypass for inference-serving pods only
3) scale up standby nodes in the same AZ and rebalance routing groups
4) if nodes continue to show ECC spikes, perform controlled driver restart + kubelet restart and mark for deeper hardware checks

emma_ops: Executing step 1-2 now. Commands:```bash
kubectl cordon ap-east-1-gpu-07
kubectl drain ap-east-1-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

ops-bot: ACTION: cordon/evac job started by @emma_ops (job_id=evac-1719994321-1)

raj_oncall: Noting: when draining, prefer live-migrate large model containers via internal router to avoid cold starts. Using weight=0 for those nodes in router.

sara_infra: Started spin-up of 5 replacement nodes in ap-east-1-gpu. Autoscaler alerted and is provisioning.

marta_eng: Quick ask for telemetry folks — capture token-level traces for endpoints  /v1/generate (sample 50) to detect degraded responses vs outright errors.

leo_sre: Running a targeted driver soft-restart on ap-east-1-gpu-07 after pods drained to maintenance NIC. Command used (on host):
```
sudo systemctl stop k3s-agent
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm && sudo rmmod nvidia_drm && sudo rmmod nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
sudo systemctl start k3s-agent
```
Note: this is less risky than full host reboot for the live evacuation.

emma_ops: Driver reload completed on ap-east-1-gpu-07. Observed one immediate Xid 31 after reload but then quiet. Kubelet restarted, then we uncordoned after healthchecks.

ops-bot: NOTE: node ap-east-1-gpu-07 rejoined after driver reload; metric 'gpu.errors.xid' dropped from 32/min to 2/min.

raj_oncall: For nodes 09 & 11 we observed persistent ECC volatile uncorrectable > 50. I'm leaving those cordoned and marking for maintenance SLA. We'll also move any replicas off those nodes.

product-support: Customer bridge is live (internal). Communicating: We are mitigating a GPU instability issue in ap-east-1; endpoints may see elevated latency or transient errors. Will update every 30m or when status changes.

marta_eng: Are there any kernel oops or segfaults inside the runtime? Need to know if it's pure hardware or memory leak.

raj_oncall: Collected runtime backtraces; one example: ```
#0  0x7f8b1c2 in alloc_tokens
#1  0x7f8b3d0 in kvcache_push
#2  0x7f90a7f in serve_loop
```
But most traces dominated by SIGKILL from OOM. Not seeing actionable heap corruption yet.

leo_sre: Next steps (post-stabilize):
- isolate affected GPUs to run memtest and stress ECC check
- update driver to latest recommended stable build across the fleet (staged canary)
- add automated circuit-breaker to route away from nodes that hit Xid > threshold for 10m
- tune cgroup mem limits for runtime workers to reduce host-level oom pressure

sara_infra: Autoscaler completed the replacement nodes, traffic rebalanced. Current cluster metrics: cpu ok, mem pressure reduced, gpu.errors.xid back to baseline on majority of hosts.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Partial mitigation successful. Impact: degraded latency for ~3% of requests and 4 customers experienced transient 503s during remediation window.

product-support: Sending summary to affected customers with ETA for root cause: investigating ECC noise and memory fragmentation; will follow up after postmortem.

raj_oncall: Switching to recovery mode. I'll hand off to @emma_ops for overnight watch and root-cause follow-up.

emma_ops: Taking handoff. I'll run overnight telemetry capture and schedule hardware tests for cordoned nodes tomorrow morning. @sara_infra please add nodes 09/11 to maintenance queue.

sara_infra: Done — nodes ap-east-1-gpu-09 and ap-east-1-gpu-11 added to maintenance queue and quarantined from autoscaler.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff: On-call changed from raj_oncall to emma_ops at 2024-06-11T22:05:10Z (incident_incident_number=INC-2024-1719994321).

marta_eng: I'll prepare an eval set to check for any quality regressions due to possible quantization/fallbacks during runtime restarts.

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Will close once hardware checks complete and Xid/ECC metrics stable for 24h.

emma_ops: Closing notes for oncall log: drained 3 noisy hosts, soft-reloaded driver on 1, replaced 5 nodes, cordoned 2 for hardware follow-up. Customer-impact window: ~00:17 - 00:47 UTC.

raj_oncall: Thanks team. If any further re-occurence, escalate to hardware vendor and open support ticket.

product-support: End of thread for now — will reopen if customers report new issues.
